full_judgment:
5. Fuli Sundari Dashi denied the plaintiffs story of taking settlement of the suit land from her. She claimed that the plaintiffs cultivated her land as her bargadars by executing Barga Kabuliyats and sometimes without barga kabuliyat and that they are in possession in respect of only 2.06 acres comprising of their homestead and tank as licensee under her. Her further case is that by registered kabuliyat dated 4 October 1948 she settled 9.57 acres land each to the father of defendant No. 2, and also to the father of defendant No. 4 and the defendant No. 3. 

 10. Trial Court upon consideration of the oral evidence of 8 PWs and 9 DWs, the documents Ext. 5, plaintiffs' amalnama, rent receipts Ext. 1(a) to 1(k), paddy receipts Ext. 2 series, certified copy of the Rent Suit Register Ext. 4, etc. and Ext. E series the registered kabuliyats of the defendants, rent receipts, SA record of right, etc, dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree as stated above holding, inter alia, that Fuli Sundari Dashi did never execute the alleged Amalnama of the plaintiffs and that Jadhu Nath was not the naib of Fuli Sundari Dashi and that the rent receipts and paddy receipts executed by said Jadhu Nath do not also relate to the suit land and that the plaintiffs could not produce the compromise decree, to connect the certified copy of the Rent Suit Register (Ext. 4) to prove that the same relates to the suit land. 

 13. The learned Judges of the High Court Division upon consideration afresh of both oral and documentary evidence on record have concurred with the finding of the trial Court that Jadhu Nath had no authority to execute plaintiff's amalnama Ext. 5, rent receipts Ext. 1 series and the paddy receipts Ext. 2 series on behalf of the defendant No. 1, and, as such, the plaintiffs did not acquire any right, title and interest on the basis of those documents and that the plaintiffs failed to connect Ext. 4, the certified copy of the Rent Suit Register with the suit land by producing the alleged compromise decree and that the defendants' names have correctly been recorded in the record-of-right and that the plaintiffs have no possession in the suit land as claimed and that in some portion of the disputed land the plaintiffs had possession as bargaders for some time of Fuli Sundari Dashi (defendant No. 1, since dead). Both the High Court Division and the trial Court have found that the plaintiffs could not prove the payment of rent in respect of the suit land and that the defendants No. 1(ka) to 1 (gha) by way of inheritance from the defendant No. 1 and other defendants on the basis of their respective Registered Kabuliyat Ext. E series dated 4th October 1948 have been possessing the suit land. It is also observed that upon transposition of the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 8 as the defendant Nos. 8 and 9 respectively the schedule of the plaint was not amended, Moreover, upon assigning cogent reasons the High Court Division has rightly refused to accept Ext. 4 Rent Suit Register as a confirmatory legal evidence of creation of tenancy in favour of the plaintiffs.
